slot.brief: Find intervals where a polynomial or rational function is increasing/decreasing by solving f′(x) > 0; requires factorisation of the derivative.

stem: The function $f(x) = \dfrac{x^2 + 2x + 5}{x + 1}$ is strictly increasing on the interval(s)
working:
By quotient rule,
$f'(x) = \dfrac{(2x+2)(x+1) - (x^2+2x+5)\cdot 1}{(x+1)^2} = \dfrac{x^2+2x-3}{(x+1)^2} = \dfrac{(x+3)(x-1)}{(x+1)^2}$.
Since denominator is positive for $x \neq -1$, sign of $f'(x)$ is sign of $(x+3)(x-1)$.
$f'(x) > 0$ when $(x+3)(x-1) > 0$, i.e., $x < -3$ or $x > 1$.
Thus $f$ is strictly increasing on $(-\infty, -3) \cup (1, \infty)$.
